profile.campus: Widows Creek, Jackson County, Alabama (former TVA Widows Creek Fossil Plant site near Bridgeport)
profile.reading: This building sits on the 360-acre former Widows Creek Fossil Plant site in Jackson County, a coal-fired power plant the Tennessee Valley Authority operated for 63 years, employing more than 500 workers directly, before shutting it down in 2015 as part of TVA's broader coal retirement program. Google announced in April 2018 it would build a roughly $600 million data center on the site, its eighth US data center and fourteenth globally at the time, with TVA committing to supply the facility with renewable power sourced from solar, wind, or hydroelectric generation to meet Google's sustainability goals rather than the coal power the site had produced for decades. Alabama and Jackson County officials framed the project as turning the economic loss of the coal plant's closure into new opportunity, and Google contributed a $100,000 grant to Jackson County schools for STEM programming around the time of the announcement; the fully built-out complex was projected to support 75 to 100 permanent jobs. Google has continued investing in the site well beyond the original announcement: in 2026 the company said it would put in an additional $1.5 billion to expand the campus through 2027, and agreed to cover the electricity its own operations consume plus infrastructure costs tied directly to the facility, a commitment TVA highlighted when it approved a 10% data center electricity rate increase phased in starting October 2026 to keep expansion costs from falling on other ratepayers. Google is also working with TVA and Kairos Power on a next-generation power source for the site: TVA plans to purchase electricity from Kairos' Hermes 2 advanced nuclear demonstration project, with up to 50 megawatts earmarked to support Google's Alabama and Tennessee data centers once that project comes online. Google's data center locations page does not publish which of the two mapped Widows Creek buildings serves which function, nor their individual square footage or MW capacity, so this registry records the campus-level investment and power figures as regional context.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center in Bridgeport, Jackson County, Alabama, confirmed through the company's own site and third-party listings. The facility's power consumption is not published. Google's disclosure policy does not include specific megawatt capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for individual buildings, so the scale of this campus cannot be determined from public sources.

Alabama has 12 mapped data center facilities, of which only 2 publish power capacity figures totaling 9.5 MW. This Google campus ranks third by published megawatts in the state, but that ranking reflects the absence of published data for other sites rather than a confirmed capacity number. No certifications, compliance standards, or technical qualifications for this facility are published.

Whether this campus matters to AI depends on information Google does not disclose. The company's aggregate state-level investment figures would show total commitment to Alabama, but campus-specific power draw, which determines actual AI training or inference capacity, remains private. Without that figure, this facility cannot be assessed against the binding constraint of compute availability.
